# Payment API returning 503 due to upstream connection pool exhaustion

Payment API sporadically returns errors; error rate climbs with traffic and recovers when traffic drops.

A new reporting job opened long-lived connections without returning them to the pool, starving the payment service which shared the same 50-connection Hikari pool.

1. Inspect HikariCP metrics to confirm active connections pinned at max
2. Identify the reporting job holding connections via pg_stat_activity
3. Move the reporting workload to a separate pool / read replica
4. Add a leak-detection threshold and connection max-lifetime

Error Details
```
HTTP/1.1 503; HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms; active=50 idle=0 waiting=37
```

Tags: database, connection-pool, hikaricp, 503, exhaustion
